taylor: Pushed a focused benchmark comparing streaming (SSE) vs non-streaming (WS/HTTP) endpoints across GPUs and regions. Goal: throughput vs tail latency tradeoffs + kernel/quantization effects. Summary below, CSV attached.
perf-bot: run_id=run-2026-03-15-18, results uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/2026-03-15/run-18.csv :white_check_mark:
ajay: can you paste the high-level numbers? p50/p95/p99 and tokens/s per GPU/region?
taylor: sure — condensed table for seq=1024, prompt length 128, payloads identical, model=redwood-7b (q4/nf4 variants)

taylor: A100(us-west-2):
  SSE  -> p50=11ms, p95=85ms, p99=200ms, throughput=5.2k tok/s
  WS   -> p50=8ms,  p95=130ms, p99=370ms, throughput=2.8k tok/s

maria: e4-96 (nvlink cluster, eu-west-1):
  SSE  -> p50=14ms, p95=120ms, p99=260ms, throughput=3.9k tok/s
  WS   -> p50=10ms, p95=200ms, p99=520ms, throughput=2.1k tok/s

ajay: RTX6000 (ap-southeast):
  SSE  -> p50=18ms, p95=160ms, p99=420ms, throughput=2.6k tok/s
  WS   -> p50=12ms, p95=280ms, p99=900ms, throughput=1.2k tok/s

taylor: pattern: SSE consistently gives higher sustained token throughput (roughly 1.8-2x) at the cost of higher p99 under bursty low-concurrency traffic. WS/HTTP has lower p50 but stalls under heavy batching due to RPC overhead.
jamie: which kernels did you run? FT vs Triton vs custom Cutlass kernels?
maria: we ran two kernel stacks per GPU: 1) FlashAttention v2 (FT) optimized path 2) Triton fused matmul-attn path. Default runtime auto-picked FT on A100, Triton on RTX6000. Differences:
  - FT: better p50 & throughput for long seqs, slightly worse p99 under preemption
  - Triton: more stable tail under low concurrency but lower peak tokens/s

perf-bot: benchmark metadata: concurrency sweep [1,2,4,8,16,32], batcher=continuous-batched, kv-cache hit ratio simulated 25%, warm-up=120s, samples=10
benchbot: raw CLI we used:
```
heybench --endpoint sse --model redwood-7b-q4 --seq 1024 --prompt 128 --concurrency 16 --kernel=auto --quant=nf4 --region=us-west-2
```

ajay: any quantization-induced quality regressions? we care about eval pass rates for q4/nf4.
taylor: quick notes: q4 (base) vs nf4 produced subtle decoding jitter. On our 10k prompt eval set (safety+factuality+instruction-follow):
  - q4 baseline: pass rate 92.3%
  - nf4 aggressive: pass rate 91.6% (delta -0.7%)
  - int8 experimental: pass rate 89.8% (delta -2.5%)

maria: measured decoding artifacts at high token-per-second regimes: SSE+nf4 increased token-drop anomalies when p99 latency >400ms; appears correlated with KV cache eviction behavior under our batching shim.
jamie: do we have a mitigation plan? pin kernel or change batching window?
taylor: proposals:
  1) region policy: route SLO-sensitive traffic to WS endpoints (lower p99 under light load)
  2) for throughput-critical background tasks use SSE with aggressive caching and FT kernel
  3) add adaptive quantization rollback: if eval-checks fail above threshold, fallback to q4 for that route
  4) tweak batching window: reduce max batch delay from 12ms -> 6ms for SSE in ap-southeast to improve tail

ajay: can we annotate which runs used soft-pinning? soft-pin seemed to improve p99 on A100 in earlier runs.
maria: yes — the runs where soft-pin=true are marked in CSV. Soft-pin reduced p99 by ~15-20% for FT kernel but cost ~6% throughput.
benchbot: attached small graph links:
  - throughput-vs-concurrency: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/bench/throughput-2026-03-15
  - p99-heatmap-by-region: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/bench/p99-2026-03-15

taylor: next actions:
  - (maria) add kernel pin experiment: force FT vs Triton on RTX6000 and run 3x sweeps
  - (ajay) sanity-check eval set for nf4 artifacts, create regression bucket
  - (jamie) draft routing recommendation for product (SSE vs WS guidance)

jamie: ack, will write a short note for product/console team. include example routing config.
ajay: leaving a TODO to re-run with kv-cache hit 0% to simulate cold-starts.
taylor: good call. re-run scheduled tomorrow at 06:00 UTC. I'll post final slides after sweep.
